name: Multilingual LibriSpeech (MLS)
description: A large multilingual corpus suitable for speech research derived from read audiobooks from LibriVox. The dataset consists of 8 languages, including about 44.5K hours of English and a total of about 6K hours for other languages (German, Dutch, Spanish, French, Portuguese, Italian, Polish). The dataset includes transcribed audio segments, language models, and baseline ASR models for all languages.
creator: Vineel Pratap, Qiantong Xu, Anuroop Sriram, Gabriel Synnaeve, Ronan Collobert (Facebook AI Research)
inLanguage: en, de, nl, es, fr, pt, it, pl
citeAs: Vineel Pratap, Qiantong Xu, Anuroop Sriram, Gabriel Synnaeve, Ronan Collobert. MLS: A Large-Scale Multilingual Dataset for Speech Research. arXiv:2012.03411v2 [eess.AS], December 22, 2020.
rai:dataCollection: Audio data was downloaded from LibriVox audiobooks using data preparation tools from the LibriLight open source library. All audio was downsampled from 48kHz to 16kHz. Text sources were obtained from Project Gutenberg and other public domain sources including archive.org, ccel.org, and hathitrust.org. For non-English languages, text extraction involved both automated parsers and manual approaches including copying text from browsers, extracting from PDF/EPUB files using pdftotext, and writing HTML parsers for popular domains.
rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Software Collection, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Audio data sourced from LibriVox audiobooks (read audiobooks in the public domain). Text sources obtained from Project Gutenberg books and other public domain websites. LibriVox and Project Gutenberg data are released in the public domain.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Numbers in text were replaced with aligned words from pseudo labels to handle variations in number pronunciation. Heuristics were applied to handle hyphens and apostrophes: rare words with hyphens or apostrophes were replaced based on alignment with pseudo labels. End-of-line hyphenation was removed and word parts were joined.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Audio files were segmented into 10-20 second segments using trained acoustic models with Time-Depth Separable (TDS) Convolutions and Auto-Segmentation Criterion (ASG) loss. Segmentation was performed by running inference to generate viterbi token sequences with timestamps, then splitting at the longest silence duration within 10-20 second ranges. Text normalization included NFKC normalization, removal of unwanted characters (punctuations, subscripts/superscripts, emojis, escape symbols), filtering characters outside valid unicode ranges based on language orthography, and removal of end-of-line hyphenation. Books with corrupted metadata, multiple speakers, or dramatic readings were removed. Only the latest version of books with the same author and title were kept. Candidate transcripts with WER >40% between pseudo label and matched text were filtered out.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human transcribers performed verification of development and test set transcripts by listening to audio files while reviewing the generated transcripts. Transcribers were instructed to correct only 'clear and obvious' errors to avoid introducing bias. Corrections included diacritic errors, missing words, and missing apostrophes.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Trained acoustic models using Time-Depth Separable (TDS) Convolutions with Auto-Segmentation Criterion (ASG) loss were used to generate pseudo labels. For English, a pre-trained model using TDS encoder and CTC loss on LibriSpeech was used. Beam-search decoding with 4-gram language models was performed to generate pseudo labels. Smith-Waterman alignment algorithm was used for transcript retrieval with matching score of 2 and substitution/insertion/deletion score of -1. TF-IDF similarity scoring on bigrams was used for document retrieval. A gender classifier (SVM with RBF kernel trained on LibriSpeech speakers, consuming 40-dimensional log-filterbank features) was used to label speaker gender with 95% test accuracy.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Gender (speaker gender was classified and used for balancing development and test sets)
rai:dataLimitations: For Polish, the out-of-vocabulary (OOV) rate is 13.39%, which negatively impacts WER when performing language model decoding with constrained lexicon. The dataset is read speech from audiobooks, which may not generalize well to conversational or spontaneous speech. For non-English languages, some audiobook text sources could not be automatically extracted due to diversity of domains and invalid links, requiring manual intervention. The pseudo-label generation approach may introduce errors that propagate to final transcripts despite filtering.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is suitable for Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) research and Text-To-Speech (TTS) research. It can be used for training, validation, and testing of ASR models. Limited supervision subsets (10 hours, 1 hour, and six 10-minute sets) are provided for low-resource training benchmarks. The dataset enables research in large-scale training of ASR systems and multilingual ASR. For English, the training set is interchangeable and complementary with LibriSpeech, with completely independent development and test sets.
